pageTitle: Klacks for Swiss Businesses | Open Source Workforce Scheduling with Data on Your Servers

hero.badge: Open Source · No licence fees · Swiss data protection
hero.titleHtml: Workforce scheduling where you stay in control.
hero.subtitle: Klacks schedules shifts automatically, optimises routes and can be controlled through an AI assistant — installed at your site, open source, with the AI model of your choice, optionally hosted locally. That way staff data stays on your own servers; the assessment under the revised Federal Act on Data Protection (revFADP, revDSG) remains with you.

challenges.title: Employment Act (ArG), data protection and the call for control

items.title: Keeping maximum weekly working hours in view
items.text: Depending on the industry, maximum working time is 45 or 50 hours a week — and the premium rules for hours beyond that statutory maximum (Überzeit) differ from group to group. Doing this by hand is error-prone.

items.title: Planning rest periods & night work correctly
items.text: 11 hours of daily rest, a maximum working span of 14 hours and a time bonus for regular night work — the Employment Act (ArG) requires complete control over every schedule.

items.title: Your own servers instead of a forced US cloud
items.text: Since the revised Federal Act on Data Protection (revFADP, revDSG), many businesses have been asking whether staff data may go into a US cloud at all — especially for AI functions.

rulesCalendar.title: A calendar for every reality
rulesCalendar.text: In Switzerland, public holidays and rules are a patchwork — different from canton to canton, sometimes even from municipality to municipality. Klacks handles exactly what simple tools get wrong.

items.title: Down to municipality level
items.text: Country, region (canton, federal state, département) and municipality — pre-configured to match.

items.title: Mix calendars
items.text: Several countries at once — for example Geneva and the USA for a business with trading partners there.

items.title: Binding or purely informational
items.text: For each calendar, you decide whether a public holiday affects hours & premiums — or simply appears as a reminder.

rulesCalendar.imageAlt: Public holiday rules in Klacks: list of a country's public holidays, each rule with its nation and region
rulesCalendar.imageCaption: Real rules from Klacks: every public holiday rule carries a country and a region, and the list can be filtered by them — freely extensible.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off Swiss businesses
solutions.subtitle: From working-time monitoring to your own infrastructure — everything works together.

items.title: Maximum weekly working hours monitored automatically
items.text: Klacks continuously monitors the 45-hour and 50-hour weekly limits for each industry and makes any breach visible immediately — on request, Klacks hard-blocks the breach in automatic planning; with manual planning it stays at a warning. The industry-specific thresholds for overtime premiums can be stored as a reference value; Klacks credits overtime premiums only as time credit and does not calculate amounts.

items.title: Rest periods planned automatically, night shifts counted
items.text: Klacks automatically factors the 11-hour rest period into planning, and the night hours that attract a premium are documented. Klacks automatically counts the night shifts in the year and warns from the 25th night — on request, Klacks hard-blocks further night shifts in automatic planning; with manual planning it stays at a warning. You document the statutory time credit yourself.

items.title: Routes & assignments optimised automatically
items.text: Klacks arranges assignments and routes so that journeys stay short and time windows are met — usable across industries.

items.title: Installed at your site: data on your servers
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure, and you choose the AI model yourself — with a locally hosted model, no AI request containing staff data goes to an external AI provider.

items.title: Klacksy: rule-based, not a black box
items.text: The built-in AI assistant Klacksy understands instructions in everyday language and controls Klacks; the plan is calculated by the rule-based planning engine — traceable through defined rules, not an opaque AI decision.

items.title: Absences covered quickly
items.text: If someone drops out, Klacks immediately shows who is qualified and available — without overturning the whole plan.

items.title: Test plan changes risk-free
items.text: Before a plan change goes live, you can run it through as an isolated copy — the 11-hour rest period under the ArG and premiums are calculated live exactly as in the real plan. Only once everything checks out do you apply the variant; until then, your live schedule stays unchanged. This lets you prepare a suitable scenario in advance for foreseeable situations — such as a staff member off sick or a peak in orders — so you are ready to act immediately when it matters, instead of improvising under time pressure. There is no artificial limit — you create as many scenarios as your planning needs.

klacksy.title: Klacksy: the built-in assistant for your team
klacksy.text: Klacksy isn't a bolted-on marketing chatbot but is embedded directly in the Klacks interface. Staff and schedulers use chat to check shift times or clarify availability. A built-in skills and rules system ensures that Klacksy makes traceable suggestions — not black-box decisions. For businesses with strict data protection requirements, the AI model can also be hosted locally.

example.title: Night work and maximum weekly working time at a glance
example.text: Klacks automatically detects when an assignment triggers the night premium or the maximum weekly working time is reached, and makes it visible straight away — no manual recalculating. On request, Klacks hard-blocks the breach in automatic planning; with manual planning it stays at a warning.
